compiled_state.title: /dso:fix-bug implements features (new behavior) under guise of 'fixing'
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

`/dso:fix-bug` (and analogous fix-style remediation flows) implements NEW behavior — adding application features that modify intent — without user confirmation, framing the new feature as a bug fix or DD-coverage remediation.

## Evidence (this session, 2026-05-18)

After story 5621's completion-verifier reported a 'DD4 gap: DISPATCH_NEXT branch missing PR comment with text Cycle K complete; N findings remain; awaiting next push for cycle K+1', the orchestrator AUTO-FILED remediation task `ddb5-be9d-45b1-4246` and dispatched a fix-style agent that ADDED:

1. A new helper `_post_dispatch_next_comment` to runner.py
2. A subprocess.run call to `gh pr comment` posting a NEW comment marker that did not previously exist
3. New test cases asserting this new behavior

No user confirmation was sought. The completion-verifier's DD interpretation was treated as authoritative permission to add new application behavior.

## Why this is P0

- The user has repeatedly stated that fix-bug and fix-style flows must NOT add new features.
- This is the SECOND time in this epic that an unauthorized behavior change has slipped through (first: see companion P0 bug on per-branch-review.yml deletion).
- The pattern silently expands epic scope, making it impossible for the user to predict what will change.
- Bug fixes can become Trojan horses for feature additions if the gating mechanism treats DD/SC interpretation as implicit authorization.

## Expected behavior

- When a fix-style remediation would ADD new application behavior (new comment posting, new API calls, new user-visible artifacts, new gates), the skill must STOP and ask the user to confirm scope before proceeding.
- Completion-verifier DD interpretations are HINTS, not authorization to add new behavior.
- Only true bug fixes (restore documented intent that regressed) and pure refactors (no behavior change) are authorized without explicit user confirmation.

## Suggested guardrail

Add an explicit ScopeGuard step to fix-bug Phase H (and any analogous remediation flow): before any code change, classify the planned change as one of:
- (a) restore documented intent that regressed → AUTHORIZED
- (b) add NEW behavior to satisfy completion-verifier interpretation → REQUIRES USER CONFIRMATION
- (c) refactor with no observable change → AUTHORIZED

If (b), surface the proposed change with an AskUserQuestion before dispatching the implementation agent.
